program_overview.title: College Mathematics Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The undergraduate core, taught the way it should have been: three academic-year tracks, placed against your actual syllabus, proofs included.
program_overview.description:
University mathematics has a famous problem: lectures move at the speed of the syllabus, not the student, and one missed fortnight of calculus compounds into a lost semester. This live online program is the counterweight. It maps the undergraduate core into three honest tracks, each one academic year long, and places every student by their current course and semester, an engineering first-year lands in Track 1 calculus, a BSc student facing real analysis lands in Track 3.

Track 1 is the first-year core: single-variable calculus done properly, linear algebra from vectors to eigenvalues, proof writing, and multivariable calculus. Track 2 is the methods year: multiple integration, ordinary differential equations and Laplace transforms, discrete mathematics, and a full treatment of probability and statistics. Track 3 is where mathematics becomes a discipline: real analysis, abstract algebra, topology and complex analysis, taught with rigorous proofs but at a human pace, with the intuition drawn before the epsilon arrives.

Each track runs 10 months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of problem practice, with up to 12 months for students who need more, the pace adapts. Assessment is honest: problem sets after every class, monthly mixed reviews that reach back deliberately, and a track exam at the end that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest for those who fall short. Real knowledge, real proofs, depth over dopamine.

faqs.question: What does the College Mathematics program cover?
faqs.answer: The undergraduate core, mapped into three academic-year tracks. Track 1: single-variable calculus, linear algebra, proof writing and multivariable calculus. Track 2: multiple integration, ordinary differential equations with Laplace transforms, discrete mathematics, and probability and statistics. Track 3: real analysis, abstract algebra, topology and complex analysis. You join the track and month that match your current syllabus, not a fixed conveyor belt.

faqs.question: Which track should I join?
faqs.answer: A short diagnostic and a conversation about your current semester decide it. Engineering first-years usually land in Track 1, second-years facing ODEs and probability in Track 2, and BSc mathematics students meeting analysis and algebra in Track 3. Since each track is joinable any month, you can also enter mid-track exactly where your university syllabus is hurting.

faqs.question: How long does each track take?
faqs.answer: One academic year: 10 months at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of problem practice, with up to 12 months for students who need more, the margin is built in deliberately. Nobody needs all three tracks at once; most students take the track their degree is currently testing them on.

faqs.question: How is progress measured? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class and come back marked with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix current topics with earlier ones so nothing fades, and each track ends with a real exam, computational and proof-based, that decides the track certificate. Falling short earns a focused revision plan and a free retest. We optimize for real mathematical knowledge, not attendance.

faqs.question: I am scared of proofs. Is this course for me?
faqs.answer: Especially for you. Proof writing is taught as its own skill starting in Track 1, with intuition drawn first and rigor layered on: read proofs, complete proofs with gaps, then write your own with line-by-line feedback. Most students who fear proofs were simply never taught them as a craft; the fear rarely survives a term of doing it properly.

faqs.question: Can this run alongside my university semester?
faqs.answer: That is the design. The tracks mirror standard BSc and engineering syllabi, so the class becomes structured reinforcement of exactly what your lectures assume. For tight semester alignment, the 1-on-1 option follows your university’s syllabus and past papers directly.

faqs.question: Is this useful preparation for graduate school?
faqs.answer: Yes, concretely: Track 3’s analysis and algebra are the core that masters admissions, entrance tests and first-year graduate courses assume, and the proof portfolio built across the program is exactly the muscle those programs test. The pure-mathematics emphasis is deliberate; methods without rigor stop working at the graduate gate.

faqs.question: What does the course cost?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 students. A mini batch of 3-4 students is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International students pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Can I try a class before committing?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Bring your current problem set; the demo is most useful when it works on your actual mathematics.

faqs.question: Are the classes live or recorded lectures?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups where problems are worked together and your written mathematics gets read and corrected in real time, never pre-recorded lectures. Mathematics at this level is learned by doing under feedback; recordings cannot mark your proof.
